label: Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae I q.5 a.1 co: A thing is GOOD_1 in a given perfection exactly…
locator: I q.5 a.1 co.: bonum et ens sunt idem secundum rem: sed differunt secundum rationem tantum
interpretation: The Catholic answer to the moral-grounding question for good: goodness is not a further property projected onto things but their being in act, desirable because perfect. Formalized per perfection as a biconditional (coextension), which captures 'the same in reality' but not the conceptual difference (good adds the notion of the desirable) or the reply's distinction between good simpliciter and good secundum quid.
